title: Avo-6-Part-3
description: Avionics Part 3 exam covering aircraft data communication, OSI and TCP/IP models, aircraft data buses, ACARS, digital modulation, network topologies, and fiber optics, with explanations based on the provided reference PDF.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct
options: A. most avionics buses are parallel
B. most avionics buses are wireless
C. most avionics buses are serial
questions.explanation: The reference notes that most aircraft data communication systems use serial transmission because it requires fewer wires.

questions.question: At a wavelength of 850 nm, what is the equivalent frequency of the source?
questions.explanation: The reference’s fiber-optics discussion uses 850 nm as an operating wavelength; its equivalent optical frequency is about 357 THz.

questions.question: Who developed a model for the connection of open systems known as the Open Systems Interconnection Reference Model?
questions.explanation: The OSI reference model was developed by ISO, the International Organization for Standardization.

questions.question: An optic transmitter consists of:
options: A. Interface circuit, source driver and optical source
B. management unit, CDU and printer
questions.explanation: The reference describes an optical transmitter as an interface circuit, source driver, and optical source.

questions.question: Which one is not true about Source Identifier (SDI)?
options: A. It identifies the source equipment
B. It is part of an ARINC 429 word
C. It can be predefined rate at which is received
questions.explanation: The SDI identifies the source of an ARINC 429 word; the keyed statement is the one that is not true.

questions.question: In aircraft, serial data transfer is achieved by:
questions.explanation: The reference explains that time-sharing is used on aircraft transmission lines; time division multiplexing provides this shared serial transfer.

questions.question: Digital modulation using phase shifting without reference is:
questions.explanation: DPSK encodes digital information by changing phase relative to the previous signal state rather than using an absolute phase reference.

questions.question: What is the ability of numerical aperture?
questions.explanation: Numerical aperture describes the light-gathering or light-collection ability of an optical fiber.

questions.question: Data communication improves safety features by:
options: B. replacing all aircraft data buses
C. reducing human error due to voice communication
questions.explanation: The reference explains that aircraft data communication reduces reliance on voice communication and can reduce crew workload and errors.

questions.question: The 4th layer in the OSI model is:
questions.explanation: In the seven-layer OSI model, layer 4 is the Transport layer.

questions.question: Laser diode undergoes light amplification by:
questions.explanation: A laser diode produces optical amplification through stimulated emission.

questions.question: ARINC 429 is a:
options: A. multiple source multiple sink system
B. single source multiple sink system
C. single source single sink system
questions.explanation: ARINC 429 is described as a simplex, single-source/multiple-sink data bus.

questions.question: Which transmission medium is unguided?
questions.explanation: Wireless transmission is unguided because the signal travels through free space rather than a physical cable.

questions.question: In which topology is a circle enclosed loop formed?
questions.explanation: A ring topology forms a closed loop, with each node connected around the ring.

questions.question: A system in which computers are interconnected and geographically spread within a building is:
questions.explanation: A LAN connects computers within a relatively limited area such as a building or site.

questions.question: Which aircraft data bus specification is used on general aviation aircraft?
questions.explanation: The reference identifies ASCB as an aircraft data bus used on general aviation equipment.

questions.question: In ISO architecture, dialogue control is the responsibility of the:
questions.explanation: Dialogue or session control is handled by the OSI session layer.

questions.question: Selection of one wavelength and leaving the other is:
questions.explanation: Optical filters can select one wavelength while rejecting or passing other wavelengths.

questions.question: Sending 1 bit of data simultaneously to different channels within the same cable is:
questions.explanation: Parallel transmission sends multiple bits simultaneously over separate channels.

questions.question: What is the maximum bit rate supported by ARINC 629?
questions.explanation: The reference lists 2 Mbps as the ARINC 629 bit rate.

questions.question: What is the word length of ARINC 629?
questions.explanation: The reference describes ARINC 629 messages using 16-bit words.

questions.question: ARINC 629 is a:
options: A. single source multiple sink bus
questions.explanation: ARINC 629 is a multiple-source, multiple-sink or multi-transmitter data bus.

questions.question: What are the operating wavelengths of fiber optics?
questions.explanation: The reference lists 850, 1300 and 1550 nm as common operating wavelengths for fiber optics.

questions.question: CSDB is a unidirectional bus that permits connection to terminals at:
questions.explanation: CSDB supports the two transmission rates 12.5 kbps and 50 kbps.

questions.question: Which network is widely used in aircraft?
questions.explanation: LANs are widely used as local networks, including in aircraft data communication environments.

questions.question: Which device is used to detect by the photoelectric effect?
questions.explanation: A photodiode detects optical energy through the photoelectric effect and converts received light into current.

questions.question: A multimode step-index fiber has a large core diameter range of:
questions.explanation: The reference gives a large core diameter range of about 100 to 300 µm for multimode step-index fiber.

questions.question: The 2nd layer on TCP/IP is:
questions.explanation: The TCP/IP model shown in the reference has Data Link as its second layer.

questions.question: How many layers does TCP/IP have?
questions.explanation: The reference states that TCP/IP has five layers.

questions.question: Which device is used to combine and split optical signals between fibers?
questions.explanation: An optical coupler combines or splits optical signals between fiber paths.

questions.question: CSMA/CA is used as media access in which ARINC standard?
questions.explanation: The reference specifies CSMA/CA as the distributed media-access method used by ARINC 629.

questions.question: What is the process of converting digital data into digital signals called?
questions.explanation: Line encoding converts digital data bits into digital signal patterns suitable for transmission.

questions.question: What is the number of receivers/sinks in ARINC 629?
questions.explanation: ARINC 629 permits up to 120 connected devices or sinks on its data bus.

questions.question: How many fields does a typical ACARS data format contain?
questions.explanation: The supplied study material keys this ACARS format question to three fields.

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly used as an optical detector?
questions.explanation: APDs are semiconductor optical detectors used in fiber-optic receivers.

questions.question: What do we call a distributed network configuration in which all data/information pass through a central computer/hub?
questions.explanation: A star network uses a shared central communication path; the wording in the question describes the bus-network configuration.

questions.question: The validity of an ARINC 429 data word is checked by using:
questions.explanation: ARINC 429 uses a parity bit to check the validity of a data word.

questions.question: Which system is used for air-ground digital data link communication and also between air carrier and aircraft?
questions.explanation: ACARS provides an air-ground digital data link for exchanging aircraft and ground messages.

questions.question: In which standard is ACARS currently defined?
questions.explanation: The reference states that the current ACARS specification was revised as ARINC 724B.

questions.question: The two types of ACARS communication method are:
questions.explanation: The reference describes two ACARS operating modes: demand and polled.

questions.question: Communication started in the cockpit is:
questions.explanation: Demand mode is the ACARS mode in which communication can be initiated from the cockpit.

questions.question: Which OSI layer handles data formatting, compression, and acts as a translator for the network?
questions.explanation: The OSI presentation layer handles data formatting and related representation functions.

questions.question: What section represents the type of information contained within the 32-bit word of ARINC 429?
questions.explanation: The Label field of an ARINC 429 word identifies the type of information represented by the word.

questions.question: One of the major differences between single-mode and multimode fiber optic is:
questions.explanation: A major physical difference between single-mode and multimode fiber is the core diameter.

questions.question: The process of superimposing a low-frequency signal with a high-frequency carrier is called:
questions.explanation: Superimposing a lower-frequency information signal on a higher-frequency carrier is modulation.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for joining optical fibers?
questions.explanation: Optical splices are used to permanently join optical fibers.

questions.question: Which is used to allow reconfiguration, typically at a termination point?
questions.explanation: A connector allows an optical or network connection to be reconfigured or disconnected at a termination point.

questions.question: A topology connection in a loop where each node has 2 neighbors is:
questions.explanation: A ring topology connects each node to two neighboring nodes, forming a loop.

questions.question: The most common protocol in the network layer is:
questions.explanation: IP is the common network-layer protocol identified in the reference’s TCP/IP discussion.

questions.question: Loss occurs due to diffraction of light when it strikes irregularities of cable during manufacturing. This is called:
questions.explanation: The supplied question is keyed to absorption loss; the fiber section discusses material/absorption losses as a source of attenuation.

questions.question: Which OSI layer determines the interface of the system with the user?
questions.explanation: The OSI application layer provides the interface between network services and user applications.

questions.question: What is the loss in signal power called as light travels down the fiber?
questions.explanation: Attenuation is the loss of optical signal power as light travels through a fiber.

questions.question: What is the primary visual instrument that the flight crew uses to access the ACARS system?
questions.explanation: The reference states that flight crew access to ACARS is usually through a CDU.

questions.question: In what type of transmission mode is communication unidirectional?
questions.explanation: Simplex transmission is one-way communication, so communication is unidirectional.

questions.question: What is the dielectric material surrounding the core called?
questions.explanation: Cladding is the dielectric material surrounding the optical fiber core.

questions.question: In the airborne ACARS system, which component manages incoming and outgoing messages?
questions.explanation: The ACARS Management Unit (MU) manages incoming and outgoing messages in the airborne system.

questions.question: The way devices are interconnected in a network is called:
questions.explanation: Network topology describes how devices are interconnected in a network.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about ARINC 429?
options: B. It is a bidirectional bus
C. It has a word length of 32 bits
questions.explanation: ARINC 429 uses a 32-bit word format.

questions.question: Which layer supports user applications like HTTP, SMTP, OSAM and email?
questions.explanation: The OSI application layer supports user-facing network applications and services.

questions.question: Which data bus uses optical fiber?
questions.explanation: The reference identifies AFDX/ARINC 664 as a high-speed aircraft data bus and describes optical implementations among modern aircraft networks.

questions.question: What is the sequence of operations in which pulse code modulation is done?
questions.explanation: PCM follows sampling, quantization and encoding to represent analog information as a digital sequence.

questions.question: Which communication medium does ACARS use?
questions.explanation: ACARS is transmitted in the VHF range; the course material identifies the aircraft communication channels in this VHF band.

questions.question: In which topology are the nodes connected to a single cable?
questions.explanation: In a bus topology, multiple nodes share a single main cable or bus.

questions.question: Which fiber is preferable for long-distance communication?
options: C. Step index single mode fiber
questions.explanation: Single-mode step-index fiber is preferred for long-distance communication because it supports low-dispersion, long-distance transmission.

questions.question: Which transmission line has an inner copper conductor and outer conductor separated by an insulator?
questions.explanation: Coaxial cable has a central conductor and an outer conductor separated by insulating material.

questions.question: Which OSI model layer implements hardware equipment?
questions.explanation: The OSI physical layer is concerned with the physical transmission medium and hardware-level signaling.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical receiver function for an optical fiber communication system?
questions.explanation: An optical receiver converts received optical energy into an electrical signal.

questions.question: What is the maximum bit rate supported by the ARINC 664/AFDX data bus?
questions.explanation: The reference states that ARINC 664/AFDX operates at 100 Mbps.

questions.question: What do we call a distributed network configuration in which all data/information pass through a central computer/hub?
questions.explanation: In a star network, devices are connected through a central hub or switching point.

questions.question: Which type of digital modulation technique is a combination of ASK and PSK?
questions.explanation: QAM combines amplitude shift keying and phase shift keying, varying both amplitude and phase.

questions.question: What does the data link layer divide the data units received from the network layer into?
questions.explanation: The data link layer packages network-layer data into frames.

questions.question: What do protocols (sets of rules) govern?
questions.explanation: Communication protocols are sets of rules that govern communication between devices.

questions.question: In which type of serial transmission are frames sent independently with start/stop flags?
questions.explanation: Asynchronous serial transmission sends frames independently using start/stop information.

questions.question: In a network, participating computers are referred to as:
questions.explanation: Computers or devices participating in a network are referred to as nodes.

questions.question: Which OSI layer performs data sequencing, where a long message is broken into smaller packets or fixed-size units for error-free transmission?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer provides sequencing and reliable end-to-end delivery functions for data units.

questions.question: Data routing is under which OSI model layer?
questions.explanation: Data routing is a Network-layer function in the OSI model.

questions.question: What is the maximum data bit rate supported by the ARINC 429 data bus?
questions.explanation: The high-speed ARINC 429 rate is 100 Kbps.

questions.question: Which topology has the highest reliability?
questions.explanation: A mesh topology provides high reliability because multiple paths can exist between nodes.

questions.question: A multimode step-index fiber has a large core diameter range of:
questions.explanation: The reference gives about 100 to 300 µm as the large core diameter range for multimode step-index fiber.

questions.question: How is error detection and correction done?
questions.explanation: Error detection/correction can use added redundancy bits so the receiver can identify or correct transmission errors.

questions.question: A system that governs message formats and rules for exchanging messages between communicating devices in a data communication network is called:
questions.explanation: A communication protocol defines message formats and rules for exchanging information between devices.

questions.question: A bus that is self-clocking is referred to as:
questions.explanation: The keyed answer is asynchronous; the supplied study material uses asynchronous terminology for transmission without a shared clock.

questions.question: Which of the following can be considered a major problem in fiber optic communication?
options: B. Its immunity to electromagnetic interference
questions.explanation: The supplied question is keyed to unidirectional operation as a major problem; the reference otherwise notes advantages such as high bandwidth and EMI immunity.

questions.question: What property does data transmission in fiber optic cable exploit?
questions.explanation: Fiber-optic transmission exploits total internal reflection to guide light through the core.

questions.question: Why is serial transmission preferred for most data transmission?
options: A. Increase in the number of wires
B. Reduction in the size and weight of cabling
C. Requirement for more copper conductors
questions.explanation: Serial transmission is preferred in many aircraft systems because it reduces the number and weight of wires required.

questions.question: In which mode does the ACARS system operate only when interrogated from the ground station?
questions.explanation: In polled mode, ACARS operates when interrogated by the ground station.

questions.question: How many maximum receivers/sinks can be connected on a single ARINC 429 data bus?
questions.explanation: A single ARINC 429 source can support up to 20 receiver/sink connections.

questions.question: Which process is adopted for laser beam formation as it undergoes light amplification?
questions.explanation: Laser light amplification is based on stimulated emission.

questions.question: A data communication network that covers a relatively large geographic area and often uses transmission facilities provided by common carriers is a:
questions.explanation: A WAN covers a relatively large geographic area and can use communications facilities provided by carriers.

questions.question: Which layer oversees delivery of a data unit between two systems on different networks?
questions.explanation: The Network layer handles delivery and routing between systems on different networks.

questions.question: What process converts analog information into a binary sequence of 1s and 0s?
questions.explanation: Pulse Code Modulation converts analog information into a binary digital sequence through sampling and quantization/encoding.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical receiver function in an optical fiber communication system?
options: B. electrical signal to optical signal conversion
C. optical signal to output electrical signal conversion
questions.explanation: An optical receiver converts the incoming optical signal into an electrical output signal.

questions.question: In which digital modulation technique does the frequency of the carrier vary according to discrete digital signals?
questions.explanation: FSK varies the carrier frequency according to discrete digital input states.

questions.question: Which protocol function finds the most efficient route between source and destination before sending the data?
questions.explanation: Data routing selects a path for data between source and destination at the Network layer.

questions.question: In which mode does the ACARS system operate only when interrogated from the ground station?
questions.explanation: Polled mode operates when the ACARS system is interrogated by the ground station.

questions.question: In which mode does the ACARS system operate when the flight crew can initialize communication?
questions.explanation: Demand mode allows the flight crew to initialize communication.

questions.question: What network technology connects machines and people within a site in a small area?
questions.explanation: A LAN connects machines and people within a relatively small local area or site.

questions.question: Which aircraft data bus standard is primarily designed for use in military aircraft?
questions.explanation: MIL-STD-1553B is identified in the reference as a military aircraft data bus standard.

questions.question: What do we call a distributed network configuration in which all data/information pass through a central computer/hub?
questions.explanation: A star network connects devices through a central hub or switch.

questions.question: How is error detection and correction done?
options: A. By changing the carrier frequency
questions.explanation: Adding redundancy bits provides information that can be used for error detection and correction.
